extract:
Nipsey Hussle, born Ermias Joseph Asghedom on August 15, 1985, was a rapper and entrepreneur from the Crenshaw district of South Los Angeles. Of Eritrean and African American descent, he came up affiliated with the Rollin' 60s Neighborhood Crips, a reality that shaped both his lyrics and his community-focused worldview. Active from the mid-2000s until his death in 2019, he became one of the defining voices of West Coast independent hip-hop in the 2010s, balancing street narratives with a sharp business mind and a Pan-African political consciousness inherited in part from his father's Eritrean roots.

He emerged through the Los Angeles mixtape circuit in the late 2000s, initially gaining traction with the Bullets Ain't Got No Name series before signing briefly to Epic Records and then Cinematic Music Group. Early influences included Snoop Dogg, Jay-Z, Tupac, and the entrepreneurial template of No Limit and Cash Money, while sonically he drew on the G-funk lineage of his city. His 2010 mixtape The Marathon and its 2011 sequel The Marathon Continues established his signature franchise — a metaphor for endurance, slow-build success, and self-determination — and tracks like "Hussle in the House" and "Bullets Ain't Got No Name" cemented his local legend.

His most discussed release before his debut album was Crenshaw in 2013, which he sold for $100 a copy in a strategy he called "Proud2Pay"; Jay-Z famously bought 100 copies. He followed with Mailbox Money in 2014 under similar terms. Throughout this period he ran his own imprint, All Money In No Money Out, eventually striking a partnership with Atlantic Records for his long-awaited studio debut Victory Lap in 2018. The album, featuring collaborators like YG, Kendrick Lamar, Diddy, CeeLo Green, and production from the likes of Mike & Keys and Mars of 1500 or Nothin', was nominated for Best Rap Album at the Grammys and is widely considered the culmination of a decade of independent grinding.

Beyond music, Nipsey was deeply invested in Crenshaw as a place. He co-founded Vector90, a coworking space and STEM incubator for Black youth, opened the Marathon Clothing smart store on Slauson Avenue, and invested in local real estate alongside his brother Samiel "Blacc Sam" Asghedom. He spoke frequently about ownership, generational wealth, and the failures of the music industry's traditional contracts, becoming a touchstone for a generation of artists rethinking distribution. His friendships and collaborations with YG (most prominently on the 2016 protest single "FDT"), Dom Kennedy, Snoop Dogg, and Roddy Ricch tied him into the fabric of contemporary L.A. rap.

On March 31, 2019, Nipsey was shot and killed outside the Marathon store; he was 33. The response was extraordinary — a memorial at the Staples Center, tributes from Barack Obama, and a posthumous sweep at the 2020 Grammys, where "Racks in the Middle" with Roddy Ricch and Hit-Boy won Best Rap Performance and "Higher," his collaboration with DJ Khaled and John Legend, won Best Rap/Sung Performance. His legacy lives on through the Marathon brand, the Nipsey Hussle Fellowship, and an enduring influence on artists who treat rap as a vehicle for ownership, neighborhood investment, and long-game thinking rather than quick stardom.
title: Nipsey Hussle
